title: Kendrick Lamar - HUMBLE.
review: Frau von Arnstein (a Viennese concert-goer, 1788): I am pleased that the voices move with propriety; the melody sits squarely on the beat; the harmonies are such as any good master would write. However, too many phrases simply stop instead of cadencing. The melody is quite memorable – I find myself humming it.

layers.text: Only the skeleton of the tune is kept (its strong-beat notes). The notes in between are re-composed as classical scale passages.
The bass is re-written as a period bass line (walking, Alberti or sustained).
The original backing is replaced by the composer's own accompaniment textures over (re-)harmonised chords.
No drums. Timpani only mark the big cadences, as in a real score.

era.name: Classical
era.summary: Clear, balanced phrases with a singable tune on top and light, transparent accompaniment, where every phrase ends in a satisfying cadence.
traits: Homophony: one main melody with accompaniment beneath
Crescendos and contrasts of mood within a movement
The string quartet and the symphony orchestra take their classic shape
era.instruments: String quartet, fortepiano, flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, horns, trumpets, timpani
why: All three eras were tried. Classical scored best (Classical 1.129, Romantic 1.117, Baroque 1.086). The score combines how classical it sounds, how much of the song survives, and how well the song suits the composer.
The song is built from regular 4- and 8-bar phrases. That matches the Classical era's balanced question-and-answer phrasing, so cadences fit naturally at phrase ends.

composer.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
composer.bio: The bridge to Romanticism: dramatic contrasts, explosive dynamics, driving rhythm and a struggle-to-triumph arc.
reasons: it is in a minor key, which Beethoven favoured for dramatic or tender music
the big jump in energy from verse to chorus suits a composer famous for dramatic contrast
applied: Inner strings murmur repeated eighth notes under the tune, the classic Viennese accompaniment
A very wide dynamic range: quiet verses and full-force choruses

ensemble.name: Orchestra
ensemble.summary: String sections plus woodwinds, horns or trumpets, timpani (and harp in Romantic style).
why: In this composer's style it scored best of the four ensembles: Orchestra 1.129, String quartet 1.104, Solo keyboard 1.101, Chamber ensemble 1.098.
Why it works: the full colour palette: the song's loud choruses can swell into the whole orchestra.
The violins i carries the vocal melody (F#4–A5). It was moved by octaves into the instrument's most singing register, with the key unchanged.

changes.ending: It follows the original beat by beat and lasts exactly as long as the clip (20.8s).
changes.dropped: The drum kit, synths and electric bass are gone. Their rhythmic drive now comes from the accompaniment patterns.
